Everything for the course is here. The **Lectures** part has one chapter per lecture day: the
definitions, results, worked examples and figures from the board. The **Seminars** part has the
problems for each seminar. Solutions with a short Python check appear after the seminar has taken place.

Under each chapter title there are links to a PDF of that chapter (for printing or reading offline)
and, for lectures, to the slides. The PDF of the whole book is under the download icon in the sidebar.

The dates and rooms are in the [Schedule](schedule.qmd).

## Grading {#sec-grading}

The course grade is on the HSE 10-point scale. Each part below is marked out of 10, and the grade is their weighted sum.

| Part | When | Weight |
|---|---|---|
| Final exam (written, all of module 3) | module 3, exam session | 45% |
| Midterm in probability (written) | module 2 | 25% |
| Attendance at seminars | modules 2 and 3 | 10% |
| Quizzes in probability (4 online quizzes) | module 2 | 5% |
| Quizzes in statistics (4 online quizzes) | module 3 | 5% |
| Seminar activity | module 2 | 5% |
| Seminar activity | module 3 | 5% |

The two exams are written in class. Each task has its points, and the total is converted to the 0–10 scale. The final exam score is not rounded.

A quiz takes 10–15 minutes from the moment you open it and covers the topics just before it. Questions are multiple choice, a short answer, or a photo of a handwritten solution. A photo is marked for whether the solution is correct and whether it is consistent and well organised, so write it the way you would at the exam. Each quiz is out of 10, and harder quizzes may count for more in the quiz grade.

Seminar activity counts the problems you solve at the board during seminars. There is no homework.

Attendance is taken at the start of every seminar. Your attendance grade is the share of seminars you attended, times 10: 9 seminars out of 14 gives $9/14\cdot 10\approx 6.43$.

If the course grade is below 3.5, you take a retake. The retake covers the whole course, probability and statistics.
